newsitem.title: UK: Seventh victim dies in British E coli outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Seventh victim dies in British E coli outbreak.

text.p: A 74-year-old man became the seventh person to die in an outbreak in Scotland of food poisoning from the E coli bacteria, health officials said on Wednesday.
All seven victims of the E coli outbreak, which has been traced to a prize-winning Scottish butcher's shop, have been elderly, the Lanarkshire Health Board said.
Several children are in hospital undergoing kidney dialysis after being poisoned by the bacteria, which can cause brain damage and kidney failure in vulnerable victims.

More than 260 people have reported food poisoning symptoms in the outbreak, which first came to light after people ate tainted meat pie at a pensioners' lunch. The health board said 119 cases had been confirmed.
E coli is a common gut bacteria that normally is harmless. But a toxic strain that lives in cattle can be passed to humans via manure or improper slaughtering.
Recent outbreaks of E coli poisoning have been reported in the United States and Japan.

More than 20 cases in Washington state, Colorado, California and Canada were linked to unpasteurised apple juice. In 1993, 500 people became ill in the Seattle area and three children died after eating undercooked hamburgers.
In Tokyo last July, 11 people, mainly schoolchildren, died and 9,500 became ill.
The British government said there had been more than 1,300 cases of E coli poisoning in Scotland since 1990.
